#1622. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Our 125 anniversary & one of the best days! 💫 pic.twitter.com/YbZLTFPpWN

I thought we showed great intensity, waited for mistakes and punished Arsenal. It was a strong performance, a very complete performance.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

I know after the international break we play every three days and a lot of the lads are not used to that. It will be tough. I hope we can compete. We have a big squad this season.

Pascal Gross pulling the strings. 🔎 @Microsoft pic.twitter.com/DAgVsG2B3W

Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions in three consecutive seasons.

Like Everton, Newcastle labour to a home win which should have been more comfortable. It would have been had Wissa scored his penalty, but it was a nervy finish as Hull pushed for an equaliser after Cho’s goal.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

One of the outstanding team performances of the season so far from Brighton, and it will take some beating between now and May. Arsenal were loose defensively in open play and from set-pieces, and were smothered by Brighton’s pressing. Arteta’s team beaten for the first time this season and emphatically so. Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

Kai Havertz shoots straight at the goalkeeper when clean through, and that is surely Arsenal’s last chance of an unlikely comeback gone. Brighton have pushed Arsenal back for much of the season half, they have not been sitting on a lead.

At St James’ Park, Hull have pulled a goal back through Cho to set up a nervy finish for Newcastle.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

What a farcical five minutes we have had, from an absurd disallowed goal for Everton to a ridiculous red card for Abdul Fatawu, banished for a second bookable offence - which was diving. There is going to be plenty said about Thierno Barry’s second goal being chalked out because, when you see it, you will wonder what it was for. These are the situations with which I struggle most - if players do not appeal for a wrongdoing, if they don’t feel they have been the victims of an injustice, why are officials getting involved?

Thierno Barry thought he had made it two for Everton, but the goal has been ruled out because Brennan Johnson was judged to be interfering with play and offside. You’re never getting those this weekend after the Enzo Fernandez incident.

Arsenal undone from a corner, swung to the back post and Chema Andres rose above everyone to head home.

This is a remarkable performance by Brighton, who have battered and bullied the champions from the start. Three-nil, and they have even beaten Arsenal at their own game by scoring a set-piece.

I am struggling to remember the last time Arsenal were overrun and outplayed as comprehensively as this. It’s a thrashing.

No half-time subs from Mikel Arteta, which is a little surprising given Arsenal’s predicament.

The undisputed highlight of the afternoon so far – Raspberry Beret has just been played during the half-time interval and you will agree that this is Prince’s finest work. We feel the need to bring this to your attention because, really, the final 15 minutes of the first half were a hotchpotch and if Everton don’t raise themselves, they will find trouble.

Another shot from outside the box as Arsenal’s defenders backed off, and the Greek striker found the bottom corner. What a first half for Brighton, Arsenal need to pull something out of the fire in the second half. Just before the goal, Saka had a chance after a deflected Odegaard shot.

Brighton’s second goal was an even better hit than their first. End-to-end football resulted in Kostoulas having space 20 yards from Arsenal’s goal. It’s another thumping low finish. Brilliant, breathless half of football by Brighton.

As half-time approaches, Arsenal have mustered just one shot on goal worth 0.03 expected goals. When they have moved the ball beyond Brighton’s press, they have not done anywhere near enough with it.

This fixture last season was especially bad-tempered, with the Brighton fans (and manager) repeatedly accusing Arsenal of time-wasting. The memories of that defeat are clearly still fresh in the minds of the Brighton supporters, who are roaring with rage at every perceived delay by the visitors, despite the fact that Arsenal are losing. The bad blood is adding to the intensity of the occasion.

Ipswich don’t play like a team that is short of confidence and quality. You might assume, if you haven’t seen much of them, that they are destined for a season of toil but there is definite quality with Gary O’Neill’s ranks, including Abdul Fatawu, who has been magnetic in drawing your eye to him. They might be a goal down but they are playing as if they are a goal in front.

Arsenal had just enjoyed a spell of control, but trail to a goal from one of the league’s in-form players. Gross whips a shot from just outside the box around Raya and in off the post.

Brighton have the lead at the Amex and it’s their captain, Pascal Gross, who has provided it. Superb long-range effort, in off the near post. On the overall balance of play, Brighton deserve that. It’s reward for their courage and willingness to go after Arsenal, rather than sitting back.

It took almost 20 minutes but Arsenal have found their feet in this game now. They are starting to find avenues through Brighton’s aggressive pressing and have made a few promising runs in behind, through Havertz and Saka. This is a high quality match.

No goals at the Amex, but Brighton are the team making the running, Arsenal struggling to play out from their own half and are yet to register a shot on goal.

Barry kept himself onside and turned the ball into the back of the net with his stomach. He did well to avoid a handball.

Bright start from Everton and they have the goal they deserve, albeit it came in fortuitous circumstances. James Tarkowski’s volley clattered into Thierno Barry and the deflection took it away from Christian Walton in Ipswich’s goal. Barry now has five goals for the season and, while he is raw, it’s an invaluable contribution.

A storming response to a bad night at Leeds from Newcastle, and it looks like being a long afternoon for Hull. Two down in seven minutes.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning important tackles.

The German was incensed by the lack of physicality and intensity in the heavy defeat to Leeds on Monday but the first goal for Joe Wilock came when Lewis Miley won a tackle on the edge of the Hull penalty box.

The second came when Sven Botman came away with the ball just inside his own half. On both occasions Harvey Barnes provided the assist. A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. Wayne Rooney is here to watch his boyhood club and he will be hoping Everton can go into the international break unbeaten. An extra special cheer too before kick-off for Jarrad Branthwaite, who has just been called up for England duty. Plenty of Premier League clubs would like to sign Branthwaite, if they were given half a chance, but David Moyes has made it quite clear that Branthwaite: “Isn’t for sale - I want to keep my best players.”

He was not part of the match-day squad at Sunderland but Ben White’s injury has opened up a place, and Dowman fully deserves it after his two goals against Ipswich in the League Cup. Sam Dean has the story of his rise to stardom as well as what Arsenal are doing to nurture such a special talent.

Brighton are wearing a special “125 anniversary” kit today, to mark 125 years since the club was formed in 1901. It’s inspired by the colours of their first ever kit, which means an all-blue shirt, pale gold shorts and dark socks. Personally I would not allow such nonsense. But I don’t make the rules.

Spurs scored two late goals to salvage some pride against Aston Villa, but it is another defeat for Roberto De Zerbi’s team who have two points from five games. This Emi Buendia screamer put the game out of reach.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

It has been a term tossed around liberally at Newcastle United since Matthias Jaissle arrived as manager, but what does “vertical football” actually mean?

It is the new buzzword in football analysis, the latest fashionable phrase to describe a “new” style of football, and it has been referenced multiple times by both Jaissle and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, since the German coach’s appointment last month.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

The right back was due to start for Newcastle against Hull City this afternoon – his first start since April – but has picked up another injury.

That will surely mean he is out of the England squad for the Nations League having also picked up a tournament-ending injury at the World Cup in the summer before the first group game.

Livramento only played 17 Premier League games for Newcastle last season, scuppering his chances of a summer move to Arsenal, missing huge chunks of the season with groin and hamstring issues.

Injuries are already cutting deep into the Newcastle squad, with four teenagers on the bench for the visit of Hull. None have played in the first team before and three of them – Michael Mills, Mason Miley and Kyrian Thompson are just 17–years-old.

Newcastle wanted a younger team this season but not this young. It was interesting to hear Matthias Jaissle talk before the game. He knows how tough this season could be with so little experience in the side.

Good news for Arsenal: Jurrien Timber is finally fit enough to start a match again. This is his first start since mid-March and his return is timely, given the absence of Ben White through injury. It’s also a first Premier League start for Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes, who comes into the midfield after his impressive performance off the bench at Sunderland last weekend.

The one he wore in Only Fools and Horses episode Yuppy Love. Of course, Bloom could actually talk about his wealth rather than one of those old five pound notes he found the other day...

Very excited for this one today. Arsenal have won all seven of their matches so far. Only once before in their history have they won their first eight games of a season - that was in 1903, when they were playing in the Second Division as Woolwich Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/iNBxoHl4Gc

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

#1621. Reading vs Bromley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:34

Reading will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Bromley to the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom in 24th.

Reading will be looking for an immediate response after suffering a 3-1 defeat to fellow promotion contenders Stockport County last weekend.

Jack Marriott equalised for the Royals after Kyle Wootton had opened the scoring, but goals from Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond ultimately earned an important victory for the Hatters.

That result saw Leam Richardson's side drop out of the playoff places, although they could return to the top six with a victory over Bromley if other results go their way.

Reading have now lost their last two league games, having also been beaten 2-0 by local rivals Oxford United, but they remain one of the most dangerous sides in the division.

The Royals have scored 26 goals in 15 league games so far, a number only eclipsed by four other teams, and the return of top scorer Marriott from injury has come as a welcome boost.

The veteran striker has scored in his last two games across all competitions and bagged a total of nine goals in 10 league games.

Bromley, meanwhile, have struggled to make the step up to League One and are bottom of the division with just nine points from 13 games.

The Ravens are without a win in their last 10 games across all competitions and new manager Karl Robinson says they "need to evolve" and "stick together" if they are to stay up this season.

Bromley's trip to Reading will be Robinson's first league game in charge, following a 2-0 defeat to Rotherham United in the FA Cup and a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons in the EFL Trophy.

It is worth noting that Bromley have never beaten Reading in a competitive fixture, although they did draw 1-1 in the EFL Cup earlier this season before the Royals triumphed on penalties.

Reading will be able to welcome back Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota from suspension and they should come straight into the side.

Marriott is expected to lead the line, with support out wide from Kyreece Lisbie and Daniel Kyerewaa.

Victor Adeboyejo remains a doubt for Bromley after he suffered an injury in the warm-up ahead of the Rotherham game, meaning Michael Cheek is likely to start up front against Reading.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller are set to continue out wide, with George Saville and Kamil Conteh starting in midfield.

#1620. Romano: Bruno Fernandes ‘more than a dream’ for Milan – why Amorim ‘could be crucial’

AC Milan could be a destination for Bruno Fernandes, who is thinking about leaving Manchester United to return to Italy.

It is no secret that Milan are looking at potential opportunities to bolster the attacking department, given the links with the likes of Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi in recent days. However, there is always the possibility that Ruben Amorim might turn to players that he already knows well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese has racked up 113 goals and 111 assists in 341 games across all competitions for United, having been their shining light in difficult recent years. He has also played in Italy before, for Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before his switch to Sporting CP.

In a video posted on their YouTube channel last night, Matteo Moretto and Fabrizio Romano discussed the possible deals that Milan could pursue to strengthen their squad, and they commented on Fernandes.

“We can’t deny that Bruno would like to return to Italy, and the idea of ​​doing so with a big club really appeals to him. It’s true that there were contacts with AC Milan this summer, but Juventus were also reportedly interested in pursuing a possible deal for the Portuguese,” Moretto began.

“In fact, Comolli, along with Bernardo Silva, also wanted to speak more in depth with Bruno, while Juve were still in contention for the Champions League, so we’re talking about the season underway. The Bianconeri made their move before the Rossoneri.”

Romano added: “Yes, Milan also made moves to try to talk to the Portuguese, also thanks to the relationship they had with Ruben Amorim at United.

“The Rossoneri remain vigilant about the Manchester captain and didn’t want to scupper this potential move because there were so many changes and developments over the summer, first and foremost with Cardinale, who is now present and has great ambition for the club.

“Another curious anecdote I want to tell you is that, and I can say this 101%, Bruno Fernandes and Amorim have an exceptional relationship. There’s great respect between the two; Bruno wasn’t even happy about Amorim leaving Manchester.

“Clearly, there’s no concrete negotiation yet. But Amorim could be crucial for the future of Bruno Fernandes, whose contract with United is currently expiring and who still doesn’t have a clear and complete idea for his future.”

#1617. Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Swiss stroll leaves serious question marks over Sebastien Pocognoli as Scots round off miserable campaign with defeat on captain Andrew Robertson's record-breaking night

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:06 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:08 EST, 16 November 2026

Despite re-establishing Scotland’s credentials as a credible football nation, by common consent, Steve Clarke’s time in charge of the side was up in the summer.

With qualification for a major tournament no longer satisfying the desires of the Tartan Army, a seven-year itch led to a parting of the ways.

In order to take that elusive step into a knock-out round, the theory went that employing a bolder coach who’d get more out of the players was all that was required. So much for that.

While few would dispute that a change at the helm was required, it was legitimate to question the wisdom in the SFA making one which was quite so radical. Those concerns have only been amplified by what’s been witnessed so far under Sebastien Pocognoli.

The Belgian is young, smart and intense. He won a title in Belgium with Union Saint-Gilloise and will have taken much from his brief, ill-fated spell at Monaco. He wants to play the kind of football supporters long to see.

But this Nations League campaign has been nothing short of dismal. Two wins from six matches, both of those coming against a poor North Macedonia side, and three nights to forget against the Swiss and Slovenia, is a lamentable record.

Andy Robertson endured a miserable night on the occasion of his record-breaking 103rd cap

Notwithstanding the fact that there were always likely to be teething problems, it’s fallen miles short of modest expectations.

Talk of it taking up to 18 months to all come up roses is all very well. But to believe that’s going to be the case, you need to see more green shoots at this point.

Having finished third in the section, Scotland are bound for pot three when the draw for Euro 2028 is made in Belfast next month.

Unless there’s a radical improvement come the qualifiers in March, it’s hard to see how Pocognoli’s side will get there by any means other than the back door.

This was another tough watch for the travelling supporters, one which will only lead to growing concerns about where all this is heading.

For half of a half, Scotland actually looked like they were getting somewhere under their new manager.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli faces some serious questions over a miserable campaign

From the minute Lewis Ferguson scored a horrible own goal, though, they became a rabble. Not nearly enough punch on the front foot. And far too easy to play through.

They shipped two goals inside five minutes early in the second half and looked like they’d have taken the final whistle there and then.

Individual mistakes from players are troubling Pocognoli in the same way they pockmarked the later days of Clarke’s reign.

Having witnessed Grant Hanley, Scott McKenna and Andy Robertson err in the World Cup, the Tartan Army had already seen Jack Hendry sent off against the Swiss at Hampden before Ferguson joined the growing list of sinners here.

Arriving midway through the first half, his unfathomable moment came when there wasn’t a red shirt in close proximity. It was a kick in the teeth for Pocognoli after a reasonable start.

While it would have been stretching matters to suggest that his team were vulnerable, Murat Yakin was without four of his big hitters in Manuel Akanji, Johan Manzambi, Dan Ndoye and Granit Xhaka.

There was a smattering of starters with five or six caps to their name. Two of the front three, Samuel Ballet and Winsley Boteli, were just 20.

Lewis Ferguson can't believe his misfortune after slicing the ball into his own net for the opener

It was a night when Scottish football history was made with Robertson winning his 103rd cap to finally rise above his great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Pocognoli stuck by the back-three – Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney – who acquitted themselves well against North Macedonia.

There was no great shock that the more defensive-minded Aaron Hickey replaced Ben Gannon-Doak on the right. Without a goal in 21 matches before a ball was kicked, Oli McBurnie’s selection ahead of Che Adams was intriguing.

The infuriating thing from Pocognoli’s perspective was that his side began with the right attitude.

Aside from an Isaac Schmidt shot which was fielded by Angus Gunn, they looked comfortable.

John McGinn’s pass into McBurnie saw the Hull forward flick the ball into space for Hickey to chase. Just when it looked like he might get a shot away, he was caught.

The positive early approach was typified by Porteous flying into a tackle 30 yards from the Swiss goal and winning the ball.

Winsley Boteli enjoys the moment after putting the stylish Swiss two goals ahead on the night

Had it not been for Hickey hesitating to pick out Scott McTominay’s run, the Napoli man would have been in on goal.

To put it mildly, the Swiss didn’t need an invitation to go down. The appropriately named Samuel Ballet was especially fond of the theatrics.

For a brief spell, Scotland had their opponents hemmed in. Pocognoli was miffed that two quick corners didn’t amount to anything.

Billy Gilmour probed and McTominay made key interceptions and sprayed passes. McGinn fired over.

At the midway point in the first half, there was much to admire. Then disaster struck.

The Swiss did well to advance down the right. Zachary Athekame simply launched a cross into the box and hoped for the best.

Aaron Hickey endured a painful injury blow and could now face another spell on the sidelines

With Ferguson running back towards goal and Porteous waiting to boot the ball to safety, there was no obvious danger.

For reasons only he could explain, the Bologna man stretched out a leg and watched on in horror as the ball sailed past Gunn. All that hard work undone in one desperate moment.

Hickey passed up a chance to immediately level when he headed Robertson’s cross wide. It was to be the Brentford man’s last meaningful involvement before he felt his hamstring tighten. Nathan Patterson replaced him.

A gift of a goal gave the Swiss a boost. Boteli launched himself at Alvyn Sanches’ cross. Gunn was untroubled.

Patterson did well to head Robertson’s deep cross back into the danger zone. McGinn’s header was straight into the arms of Yvon Mvogo.

For all Scotland were entitled to feel a little sore at being one down at the break, it could have been worse. The defence were completely static as Adrian Bajrami launched himself at a header. It was a good thing, from Gunn’s point of view, that the defender missed the target.

Alvyn Sanches drills home Switzerland's third goal in what was an entirely one-sided contest

Ferguson truly had a night to forget here. Within two minutes of the restart, he needlessly invited pressure when he launched a ball straight out of play.

Within seconds, with Porteous advanced, the Swiss broke down the left. Ballet fed Remo Freuler who returned the favour. Ballet rolled the ball towards goal from 12 yards with Boteli claiming the final touch. The visitors’ hopes of a VAR reprieve for offside were dashed.

And with that, the roof caved in. Patterson was dispossessed and Boteli worked the ball into the feet of Sanches. You could only admire the finish, but Scotland were an absolute mess in the build-up. It was threatening to get ugly.

With Tierney, Scotland’s best player on the night, lying on the deck, Ballet was only denied by Gunn. The Tartan Army looked at the clock and wished it was over.

With a minute remaining, a bad night got worse when Zeki Amdouni’s deflected shot beat Gunn.

Mercifully, this tortuous Nations League campaign can now be consigned to history. It’s been the most chastening experience for all concerned.

#1615. Opinion: Julian Ward will sign €30m South American wonderkid for Liverpool

Julian Ward has been thrown into the deep end as Liverpool's sporting director.

Over the last couple of windows, the Reds' transfer regime has been handled by Richard Hughes.

The Englishman managed to spend well over £600 million during his time as the Reds' sporting director and, after managing to make the team worse despite this huge amount of spending, he chose to pack his bags and leave for pastures new.

This left Liverpool looking for a new person to take the reins with Fenway Sports Group eventually landing on Julian Ward as their preferred option.

Since then, the rumour mill has been in overdrive and now that we're edging closer to the transfer window opening back up, some of these links are going to have to turn concrete and actually get completed.

Liverpool want to sign Arthur Dias from Athletico Paranaense

One of the main transfer strategies that Liverpool have had over the last couple of years is signing young players for the future.

They've always had one of the best academies in the world but now, they're clearly looking for more ways to set themselves up.

So far, most of their transfers have worked out and, while the jury is still out for some of them such as Milos Kerkez, they're all still incredibly young and have a lot of their careers left to go.

But, as much as Liverpool have youngsters among their ranks, they also have some veterans who many need replacing in the future.

As mentioned, many different players have been linked with Liverpool but now, thanks to an update from FussballEuropa, Brazilian centre-back Arthur Dias has been linked.

"Liverpool FC has its eyes everywhere – including on the Brazilian market. The Reds' scouts are keeping a close eye on Arthur Dias. The race for the talented center-back is already on," they wrote.

"Athletico Paranaense could have made a significant sum from Arthur Dias last summer. Tottenham Hotspur showed concrete interest and reportedly submitted an offer of just over €20 million.

"However, this was too low for Paranaense, and consequently, no deal was reached.

"Dias has even earned two caps for the Brazilian national team. This automatically makes the rising star a target for other clubs. According to information from Fussballeuropa.com, Premier League side Liverpool are keeping a close eye on Dias.

"The Reds are regularly monitoring the young defender and keeping a close eye on his development.

"As Fussballeuropa.com has also learned, Paranaense are demanding a transfer fee of at least €30 million. The 2001 Brazilian champions will reportedly not even enter negotiations for anything below this magic number."

Dias is probably a player that hardly any Liverpool fans have heard of.

But, the fact that he's 21 years old and has already been given two international caps for Brazil proves how good he actually is.

The centre-back is one of the most highly-rated prospects in the Brazilian Serie A and, the fact that he's available for around £25 million is mad.

Obviously, the step up from the Brazilian Serie A to the Premier League will be a big one but, since Jeremy Jacquet managed it, there's no reason why Dias can't too.

Many transfers are likely to be made by Liverpool in 2027 but, if Dias isn't one of them, they'll be leaving themselves rather red-faced.

Here's hoping that Ward and Andoni Iraola can align their transfer values and bring Dias in.

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:59

Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.

The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league following a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.

After securing a record-extending 56th Scottish top-flight title on a dramatic final day of the season in May, Celtic began the 2026-27 campaign hoping for more of the same, retaining Martin O'Neill as manager, who will take charge of his 339th game at the helm this weekend.

While they currently sit top of the Scottish Premiership with a four-point cushion over arch-rivals Rangers, their season has been far from straightforward, with the Bhoys entering the international break having recorded just one league victory in their previous three outings.

A home draw against Dundee United was followed by a defeat away to Falkirk, their first loss to the Bairns in nearly two decades, before they were presented with an opportunity to return to winning ways against basement side Kilmarnock, although their eventual 1-0 victory was far from convincing.

O'Neill's side took the lead through Republic of Ireland international Liam Scales but were made to work hard for all three points against a team that has won just twice all season.

Celtic have struggled even more in Europe, with just one victory from their opening four Europa League matches leaving them 32nd in the 36-team league phase and facing an uphill battle to reach the knockout stages.

Meanwhile, St Mirren have endured a difficult spell since their 2-1 defeat to Celtic in September, losing seven of their subsequent nine league matches and collecting fewer points than any other side in the division during that period, although their early-season results have at least kept them clear of the bottom two.

Led by Craig McLeish, who took charge on a permanent basis in June, the Buddies have won four, drawn two and lost seven of their opening 13 league fixtures, with the teams below them potentially able to close the gap through games in hand.

While they secured a narrow victory over Dundee in October, St Mirren have collected just one point from their subsequent three top-flight outings, extending their disappointing run of form.

The appointment of a young manager with ambitions of introducing a progressive style of football has yet to produce the desired results, with the Buddies' 12 goals scored representing the lowest total in the division, while their 22 conceded is the second-highest.

After beating Kilmarnock 1-0 in early September, St Mirren sat second in the table with 10 points from a possible 12, but collecting just four more across their next nine matches has brought their promising start to a halt, although that early form provides a platform for McLeish's side to build on if they can rediscover their confidence.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, Celtic had several players away on international duty over the past fortnight and may need to make changes depending on their fitness following the additional travel.

Auston Trusty recently took a break from football following the death of his father and has not featured for O'Neill's side since their 4-1 Europa League defeat to Benfica in October.

However, he scored for the USA against Haiti during the international break and dedicated his goal to his father, potentially putting himself in contention for a return this weekend.

Alistair Johnston would have travelled to North America to join up with the Canada squad but remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained during a 2-1 victory over Hibernian at the end of October.

The Canadian full-back and German midfielder Mika Baur are O'Neill's only expected absentees, although it remains to be seen whether Kasper Hogh will retain his place up front after failing to score for the 16th consecutive match last time out.

As for St Mirren, they could name the same starting XI for a second consecutive match, although McLeish may be tempted to make changes following the two-week break.

Nikolas Agrafiotis, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus have all been sidelined through injury but are expected to return in the coming weeks, with Saturday potentially coming too soon for some of the trio.

Jonah Ayunga is also unavailable through injury and is not expected to return until early 2027.

#1609. Report: Liverpool set transfer strategy to sign £45m star

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players recently.

The Anfield outfit are massively underperforming with fans demanding that replacements for a decent chunk of their players are sourced in the upcoming transfer windows.

Long-term links with Alex Scott and Adam Wharton have remained while new rumours with players such as Arthur Dias have now started to emerge.

However, before the January transfer window even opens, there are a couple of deals that already feel close to completion.

And now, the Reds seem to have created a transfer strategy to get one deal done.

Liverpool want to negotiate Ronald Araujo's price down before signing him

Right now, Ronald Araujo is probably Liverpool's best-performing summer signing.

The Uruguayan came to Anfield on a season-long loan with a €55 million option to buy.

And, even though he's been one of their best defenders, his injury history and age are a cause for concern.

Whether he's been used as a right-back or a centre-back, he's always done well and has certainly helped solidify Liverpool's back line.

At the moment, Liverpool are more than pleased with Araujo's contributions but, according to an update from Diario Sport, they're not willing to sign him permanently unless they can knock his price down a bit.

"Liverpool want to keep Ronald Araújo, but not at any price," they wrote.

"The English club is very pleased with the Uruguayan center-back's performance, on loan from Barça until the end of the season, although they don't intend to automatically exercise the €55 million purchase option agreed between the two clubs. Their aim is to negotiate a lower fee.

"Liverpool's strategy is to wait until the end of the season to sit down and negotiate with Barça. The Anfield management considers €55 million too high and are confident they can reduce it considerably.

"Liverpool intends to leverage the player's contract situation and high salary to put pressure on Barcelona in negotiations. Barcelona will have to decide whether to accept a lower fee than initially agreed or bring back a player who is proving his worth in the Premier League."

Liverpool signing Ronald Araujo for cheaper than €55 million would be ideal

As mentioned, Araujo has been in fine form this term.

The defender has been a revelation at Anfield but, the €55 million fee is obviously quite steep.

So, if Liverpool manage to knock the price of the defender down and Barcelona agree to sell him, they'll be in the money.

The fact that Araujo can cover both positions is one of his main selling points with versatility being a key part of football in this day an age.

Obviously, the fact that he's got plenty of Champions League experience and will have a year of Premier League football under his belt is also a major selling point.

There's no mention of how much Liverpool would want to pay for Araujo but, if it's anywhere near €35 million - €40 million, it would be an absolute steal.

#1608. Scaroni explains Cardinale’s ‘long-term’ project and why stadium is ‘fundamental’ for success

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

As we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has big plans to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The new ‘MSE’ holding company is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

Serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

“You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

“So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

“This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this…

“Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

“The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

“This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

“Building a great stadium like this is something extremely important. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this company that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

“So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this new stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this new stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European company – but I would also say worldwide.

“They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the new stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

“Naturally, as always with these issues, there may be some discussion points. Furthermore, in Milan we’re heading towards an election campaign for a new mayor, and a topic like the construction of a new stadium is one that can naturally excite politicians.

“Let’s say we’re confident because the entire process we’ve taken so far protects us from these potential disruptions, and we’re fiercely determined to move forward. With the new stadium, among other things, we’ll have €100 million in additional revenue.

“This €100 million in additional revenue is a fundamental ingredient for the success of AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Serie A around the world, because ultimately, €100 million – to have great players, to pay great players – is a fundamental ingredient for success.”

#1607. Opinion: Andoni Iraola dealt transfer blow, €90m deal won't happen

Andoni Iraola was sort of thrown in the deep end when he took over from Arne Slot as Liverpool's manager.

The Reds were coming off the back of a fifth-place finish in the Premier League, a result which ended with Slot being relieved of his duties.

Fenway Sports Group knew that they had to get their next appointment right which is why fans were so happy with the Spaniard being appointed.

His heavy metal style of football and his previous Premier League experience looked like two of the main reasons why he was perfectly suited to the role.

However, since his appointment, things have been a bit topsy-turvy with Liverpool even losing to Fenerbahce in the Premier League.

This caused many questions to arise with the upcoming transfer windows now seeming rather important.

Atletico Madrid will not sign Martin Zubimendi which could stop Pablo Barrios from joining Liverpool

Liverpool's midfield is one of their main problem areas at the moment.

Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni have done a stellar job but, since neither of them can play every single game, others such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have been called upon.

And, even though both of those players were handed new long-term deals last term, they just can't seem to get the hang of playing in a double pivot.

This realisation has dawned upon Liverpool recently which is why Atletico Madrid midfielder Pablo Barrios was linked with a move.

Of course, it was just a rumour but of all the midfielders mentioned, Barrios felt like a rather exciting option.

However, thanks to a fresh update from journalist Matteo Moretto, Liverpool's move for Barrios seems to have just hit a major roadblock.

"Martín Zubimendi is not a financially viable target for Atlético Madrid ahead of the winter transfer window," he shared via X.

"Arsenal would demand a fee of over €70 million, and the Gunners intend to keep him despite Chelsea’s interest.

"Martin Zubimendi is not on Atlético’s radar at the moment."

Liverpool may have to turn their attention towards Lamine Camara again

Liverpool have been linked with new midfielders ever since Fabinho left.

The Brazilian was the Reds' last natural number six and, since he hasn't been replaced yet, the Anfield outfit are still on the lookout for new talent.

Many different players have come close to joining Liverpool with Lamine Camara being one of their most-linked players in the summer.

Obviously, that deal never came to fruition but, since the Senegal international didn't move to another club, talk of him being of interest to Liverpool has emerged again.

During his time with AS Monaco, Camara has become one of their most important players and, thanks to this, their asking price for him has sky-rocketed.

However, with Liverpool's options for new midfielders now dwindling, their deal for Camara may have to be back on, even if he is going to cost an arm and a leg.

#1606. Tottenham Hotspur vs. Ipswich Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 15:09, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 15:10

Separated by three places in the Premier League table, 12th-placed Tottenham Hotspur welcome Ipswich Town to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday seeking a return to winning ways on matchday 11.

Leeds United halted Spurs' three-match league winning streak before the hiatus, and the capital club now aim to begin a seemingly favourable run of fixtures with a positive result against the Tractor Boys.

Roberto De Zerbi could have been forgiven for entering the international break disappointed after Leeds ended his side's three-match winning run at the start of the month.

Spurs scored seven goals and conceded just once across victories of 3-1, 2-0 and 2-0 over Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace to close out October, following a creditable 1-1 draw with 10 men at Manchester United.

Returning to home comforts in the capital presents an ideal opportunity for the Lilywhites to regain winning momentum as they pursue a third consecutive triumph in front of their supporters after victories over Coventry and Palace.

The upcoming schedule will quietly please De Zerbi, whose team face Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Hull across their next five matches, offering encouragement ahead of those encounters with bottom-eight clubs.

Having already collected eight points from a possible 12 against the other four sides in the bottom eight, Spurs, currently four points behind fifth-placed Chelsea, will target another victory that could lift them into the division's top half.

Overcoming Ipswich will be far from straightforward for the North Londoners, despite the Tractor Boys winning only one of their last six Premier League matches and losing three.

The defeats suffered by Gary O'Neil's men against Everton, Manchester City and Bournemouth have all been narrow, underlining their battling qualities.

With their other two matches outside a 2-1 home victory over Fulham producing draws against Nottingham Forest (1-1) and Hull City (2-2), the travelling supporters will hope for another competitive showing from the promoted side.

That ambition is tempered by Ipswich collecting just four points from a possible 15 away from home this season, although O'Neil's men have recovered from a 5-2 gameweek two thrashing at Manchester United to beat Palace 3-2 and draw 2-2 at Hull, either side of defeats of 1-0 at Everton and 3-2 at Man City.

Although they have conceded at least twice in four of their five away matches since returning to the big time, the travelling supporters will back their side to secure a positive result if they deliver another spirited performance outside Portman Road.

Spurs have several injury doubts ahead of this weekend's match, with Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Martin Dubravka (knee), Savio (muscle), Mathys Tel (ankle), Lucas Bergvall (knee) and Tosin Adarabioyo (calf) facing assessments, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain sidelined with knee problems.

Mohammed Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, but the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

No Spurs player has scored more league goals than Jan Paul van Hecke, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back ahead of Saturday's encounter with the Tractor Boys.

O'Neil's side, meanwhile, have five players with two goals apiece: Emersonn, Jack Clarke, Julio Enciso, Leif Davis and Zian Flemming.

While Flemming has yet to start for the visitors, with Emersonn generally preferred at centre-forward, the former Burnley man's two away goals make him a potential game-changer off the bench in North London.

Unlike Spurs, who have several injury doubts, the visitors are believed to have a healthy squad for their gameweek-11 trip to the capital.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Gray, Marmoush; Solanke

Walton; Greaves, O'Shea, Diop; Ouattara, Lukic, Palacios, Davis; Maeda, Enciso; Emersonn

Ipswich have scored four goals across their last two away matches, offering encouragement that their varied attacking threats can trouble a Tottenham side carrying several fitness concerns.

Nevertheless, the visitors' inability to keep opponents quiet on their travels should provide enough opportunities for Spurs to secure another home success.

#1605. GdS: Milan choose Tresoldi with Club Brugge star desperate for move – the situation

AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

The newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter. Part of the reason for this is because Endrick – the alternative name – made his intentions clear: “I hope to spend my life at Real Madrid.”

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In this story of preferences, Tresoldi’s choice is also crucial. The 22-year-old has supported Milan since he was a child, while in Belgium and beyond he has proven himself to be a goal scorer. Inter found this out, as he scored a hat-trick against them in the Champions League at San Siro.

The No.9 shirt and role is currently occupied by Gonçalo Ramos, not a trivial thing due to the record-breaking fee paid for him last summer. However, Ruben Amorim genuinely believes the Portuguese can co-exist with Tresoldi, who can be on hand to finish the chances created by Ramos’ movement.

Tresoldi is a true ‘devil’ in the penalty area. He has 18 goals this season for club (eight in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Belgian Super Cup) and another four for Germany’s U21s. This leaves him just shy of 20 goals, in mid-November.

Tresoldi is also desperate to move to Milan and if it were up to him, the deal would be done. His desire to join his boyhood club could prove helpful and provide a boost to the deal’s success, just as it has before. His agents and family are equally positive about a potential Italian move.

Club Brugge are in a different mood, however, and would happily keep him unless offered at least €60m. Just a few months ago, the Belgian giants rejected offers just over half that. This is a figure Milan are willing to negotiate around, because Champions League qualification is crucial and goals are needed to achieve this.

Besides, Cardinale is of the opinion that it’s better to invest now than risk deepening the deficit. Another year without the revenues from the top club competition would be far from ideal for many different reasons.

What about Francesco Camarda? Here too, the debate is over: the club and the coach agree on the need for a loan, perhaps abroad. Camarda agrees: he knows he needs to regain rhythm by playing regularly, to help his development.

For Milan, it would be another negotiation with Brugge after Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. The deal for the former was conducted by Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara, while for the latter it was Igli Tare. Now, Cardinale intends to do things himself.

The owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

#1604. Opinion - Liverpool must be brave: Reject Barcelona star

Liverpool have got to be brave. It's time to fully reject a Barcelona star and move on to something new.

Liverpool have some major decisions to make over the next few months. They've got to lock in their transfer targets, not just for January but for next summer, too.

And this is a squad that needs transfers. That's the sad reality of things - there's just too much uncertainty for Liverpool to stick with what they've got, even after spending record-breaking amounts.

Centre-back is a problem, with Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez both out of contract. Ronald Araujo is only on loan, too. Jeremie Frimpong doesn't appear to have a future at right-back, either, and Conor Bradley is an unknown quantity post-injury.

Left-back is a difficult one, too. Milos Kerkez is still establishing himself, and Kostas Tsimikas is out of contract. This is the area where difficult decision no.1 can be made, though.

The Alejandro Balde problemLiverpool will need to sign a left-back and they've been consistently linked with Alejandro Balde. The player isn't getting proper game time at Barcelona and is viewed by many clubs as the best possible option on the market. After all, he's still young at just 23, has incredible experience, and his attacking numbers stack up very nicely. However, we're going to argue that this is one Liverpool should pass on. Balde would apparently cost €40m. It's a fairly large amount of money for a left-back - Kerkez is the only player Liverpool have spent more than €15m on in the position.

Liverpool will need to sign a left-back and they've been consistently linked with Alejandro Balde. The player isn't getting proper game time at Barcelona and is viewed by many clubs as the best possible option on the market.

After all, he's still young at just 23, has incredible experience, and his attacking numbers stack up very nicely. However, we're going to argue that this is one Liverpool should pass on.

Balde would apparently cost €40m. It's a fairly large amount of money for a left-back - Kerkez is the only player Liverpool have spent more than €15m on in the position.

It's especially a large amount of money for someone who isn't even playing regular football at this point. It's also far more than most clubs are actually paying for their left-backs.

Bournemouth, for instance, spent just €14m signing Adrien Truffert to replace Kerkez in 2025. He's now a left-back that everyone wants - but it isn't like he was hiding anywhere. He was one of the best-rated in France.

So given the investment in Kerkez already, it seems a little mad to spend a substantial amount on a new left-back. Surely the risk this time should be on a lower-cost player? Especially as Balde would command risk anyway as a player Barcelona aren't all that keen on.

#1603. Kilmarnock vs Aberdeen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 15:30

Kilmarnock and Aberdeen face off in an early relegation six-pointer in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday at BBSP Stadium Rugby Park.

Killie are rock bottom in the Scottish Premiership table with nine points from 12 matches, while Aberdeen are just two points and one place above them.

Kilmarnock have shown glimpses of a promising side under Neil McCann, but their reckless defending is proving to be a major stumbling block.

They have managed just two wins in 13 league matches, losing eight of those encounters, and are enduring a particularly difficult spell, having suffered three defeats in their last four outings.

Killie have scored 13 goals this season, showing that they possess the attacking threat to trouble opponents, but their defensive frailties are turning into a recurring nightmare.

McCann's side have conceded 29 goals so far, more than any other team in the division, and unless they address that problem, climbing the table will become an increasingly difficult task.

The East Ayrshire club have won just once in their last seven matches, while their home form has been particularly poor, with only five points collected from six games and 15 goals conceded.

Earlier this week, Aberdeen appointed Mario Frick as their new head coach following the dismissal of Stephen Robinson.

There is an acute sense of instability at the club, with the former Liechtenstein striker becoming their fourth manager in 2026, following Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin.

Frick guided Vaduz to promotion in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation in 2021, and he will need to work similar magic at Aberdeen as the club look to navigate their current crisis.

The Dons have lost four consecutive matches across all competitions and managed just one victory in their last six Scottish Premiership outings.

Aberdeen have collected only four points on the road this season, but they have lost just once to Kilmarnock in their last six meetings across all competitions.

McCann does not have any major injury concerns, with goalkeeper Maksymilian Stryjek his only absentee.

The 30-year-old is currently sidelined with a knee injury but is expected to return by the start of next month.

It will take time for Frick to get a better understanding of his squad, but his immediate priority will be to motivate the players and prevent another defeat in this crucial encounter.

The Dons, meanwhile, are without Lewis Mayo (foot), Chris Cadden (hamstring), Kristers Towers (knee), Emmanuel Gyamfi (thigh) and Mats Knoester (tendon), although all five are expected to return by the middle of next month.

#1602. Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

🗣️ "We started to tire in the second half"Millwall manager Alex Neil shares his thoughts on this afternoon's Dockers Derby, after the Lions drew 2-2 with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/xnmubZ9NIz

🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... Obviously I’m so far away it’s hard for me to see what happened, but I wouldn’t presume that Fil would say that without cause.

“I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”

"It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever played in..I got shivers walking out"Millwall's Caleb Taylor speaks to Aaron Paul following today's 2-2 draw with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/yFoRuxooe6

Will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

Millwall 2 West Ham 2 (Mavropanos) Millwall are finally undone by a cross. Bowen goes short with a corner and Solomon dinks the ball on to the Greek defender’s head and he plants the ball past Marschall. The away end erupts...

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

It’s Bowen’s turn to try an effort at goal. Metcalfe does brilliantly to charge it down but there is no respite for Millwall as Kante’s long-range sighter goes behind for another corner.
